title: Client onramp prioritization rubric — language coverage, auth patterns & streaming ergonomics
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: We receive a steady stream of customer requests for new language client libraries and auth/streaming ergonomics changes. Without a consistent intake and prioritization rubric we over-index on vocal requests and create engineering churn. This ticket defines a repeatable rubric and intake flow for triaging SDK/client requests with a focus on enterprise needs (auth patterns, token rotation, SSO/OIDC, resumable streaming, backpressure) and language coverage trade-offs.

Goal: Establish a lightweight scoring rubric, an intake form, and a small gating checklist so PM/Eng/Design can rapidly decide: Build native SDK, provide official adapter, or document a community pattern. Deliverables:
- Prioritization rubric (weighted scores and thresholds)
- Intake form template for Solutions/Support/AE to capture signals
- Triage runbook with owners and SLAs (48h acknowledge, 10 business days initial decision)
- Example triage outcomes for 3 representative customer asks (PHP client for streaming inference; Rust production client with mTLS + token rotation; mobile JS with resumable reconnect)

Scope (what this ticket covers):
- Language coverage decision criteria (usage signals, revenue linked customers, engineering cost, runtime compatibility)
- Auth pattern requirements: token refresh flows, client credentials, SSO/OIDC federation, mTLS for private deployments, KMS/HSM considerations for Private customers
- Streaming ergonomics: reconnect/resume semantics, backpressure and chunked responses, metadata propagation, idempotency and delivery guarantees
- Non-goals: Implementation of any single SDK (those will be follow-up tickets if rubric leads to build)
acceptance_criteria: 1) A published rubric doc exists in Confluence and linked from the SDK intake playbook. 2) Intake form created in Zendesk/Forms and sample submitted by Support team. 3) Triage SLAs documented and agreed with Eng and Design. 4) 3 example customer requests scored and decisions recorded (adapter / build / decline). 5) Roadmap signal bucket and handoff template for follow-up tickets.
scoring_rubric: Scoring axes (0-10 each) with weights: customer_count (weight 1.5), revenue_impact (2.0), platform_alignment (1.0), engineering_cost_est (in dev-weeks inverted to score) (1.5), security_compliance_need (2.0), maintenance_risk (1.0). Final score = weighted sum. Thresholds: >=30 -> Build official SDK; 20-30 -> Official adapter + docs; <20 -> Guidance + community template. Example: PHP streaming client for transcription request (customer_count=6,revenue=8,platform_alignment=6,eng_cost=4,security_need=3,maintenance=5) => final=~29 => adapter + prioritized docs.
intake_form_template: Fields to capture: company_name, customer_tier, primary_contact, brief_use_case, estimated_monthly_requests, required_auth_modes (API key, OAuth client, SSO/OIDC, mTLS), streaming_requirements (resumable=true/false, max_chunk_ms, backpressure_behavior), required_regions, compliance_constraints (SOC2, HIPAA, FedRAMP), deadline/launch_date, business_impact_metric. Also ask for a reference app or example payloads and a contact willing to participate in early testing.
runbook: Triage runbook: 1) Triage owner (PM oncall) acknowledges request within 48h. 2) Triage meeting cadence: daily async scoring; weekly sync with Eng and Design for borderline items. 3) Required inputs before decision: sample traffic profile, security requirements, expected QPS, compatibility constraints (mobile/embedded). 4) Outcome templates: Build (create ENG- ticket + design spike), Adapter (create PM task + docs owner), Defer (log in backlog with signal tags). 5) Escalation path: if security_compliance_need >=8 escalate to Security for gating review. SLAs: initial decision in 10 business days, prioritized scheduling within next roadmap cycle depending on score.
